issues.description: Check class name and metadata CheckID do not match the directory/file naming convention
issues.detail: The PR description, branch name, and CHANGELOG entry refer to 'compute_instance_multiple_network_interfaces', but the directory, files, class name, and metadata CheckID are all 'compute_instance_single_network_interface'. The framework's contract for a check requires that the directory name, the .py filename, the class name inside it, and metadata.CheckID all agree — this is the substitution point the loader relies on. Here they do agree internally (good), but the PR title/description disagree. Confirm which naming is intended and align CHANGELOG plus PR title; otherwise downstream consumers searching for the documented CheckID will not find it.

issues.description: MANUAL status is undocumented in metadata and contract; introduces a third state without spec
issues.detail: The check's docstring promises three outcomes (PASS / MANUAL / FAIL), but the metadata.json describes only PASS/FAIL semantics and the framework's Check contract historically returns PASS/FAIL. Introducing a MANUAL status changes the postcondition of execute() — callers and downstream aggregators that switch on status may not handle MANUAL. Either state MANUAL explicitly in metadata and verify Check_Report_GCP/aggregation supports it as a first-class status, or replace the GKE branch with PASS plus a clarifying status_extended.

issues.description: GKE detection by name prefix is a leaky, brittle heuristic embedded in the check
issues.detail: Identifying a 'GKE-managed instance' by `instance.name.startswith('gke-')` leaks naming convention from one Google product into the abstract data type of Instance. Users can name any VM 'gke-foo', and real GKE node-pool prefixes are configurable. The right boundary is to add an `is_gke_managed` (or a label/metadata-derived) attribute on the Instance ADT computed once in compute_service, with the rule stated as a postcondition; the check then queries the abstraction rather than re-implementing detection. As written, every future check that wants to exempt GKE will re-derive this rule inconsistently.

issues.description: NetworkInterface ADT is anemic relative to data already parsed in _get_instances
issues.detail: The new NetworkInterface model captures name/network/subnetwork but discards accessConfigs/natIP, which _get_instances already iterates to compute `public_ip`. This creates two parallel representations of the same upstream object: a derived boolean (`public_ip`) and a partial list (`network_interfaces`). Future checks (public IP per NIC, NAT presence, alias IP ranges) will either re-parse the raw API or duplicate this loop. Recommend extending NetworkInterface with `access_configs` / `has_public_ip` and deriving the instance-level `public_ip` from the list, so the ADT is the single source of truth.

issues.description: Invariant on network_interfaces is not stated; zero-NIC branch silently passes
issues.detail: The check handles `interface_count == 0` by leaving status=PASS with a 'has no network interfaces' message. Whether a GCE Instance can have zero network interfaces is a real invariant question (the API does not normally allow it). Either state the invariant on the Instance ADT (`len(network_interfaces) >= 1`) and treat zero as an internal error, or define the postcondition explicitly. Silently passing an impossible state hides bugs in the service layer.

issues.description: NetworkInterface.network/subnetwork lose the URL frame without documenting it
issues.detail: The service strips network/subnetwork to the last path segment (`.split('/')[-1]`). That is a lossy transform on the ADT: project and region context are discarded, and two subnetworks named 'default' in different VPCs become indistinguishable. If this is intentional for display, document it as a postcondition on the field; if checks will need fully qualified URIs (e.g., cross-VPC reasoning), preserve the original `self_link` form and let consumers shorten when rendering.

issues.description: Test for zero network interfaces is missing
issues.detail: The test suite covers single, two, multi, mixed, GKE-multi, and no-instances, but does not exercise the `interface_count == 0` branch in the check. Given that branch is reachable in the code and changes status_extended, the contract is under-tested. Add a test or remove the branch in favor of an asserted invariant.

review.summary: The check is internally consistent — directory, filename, class, and CheckID all agree on 'compute_instance_single_network_interface' — but the PR title, description, and CHANGELOG narrative use 'multiple_network_interfaces', so the documented contract and the shipped artifact disagree at the boundary callers will search. Below that, the abstraction has two real weaknesses: a new MANUAL status is introduced without being stated in metadata or (visibly) supported by the Check_Report contract, and the 'is this a GKE node' rule is encoded as a name-prefix string match inside the check rather than as a property of the Instance ADT — a leak that the next check will duplicate inconsistently. The new NetworkInterface model is a good move toward a richer Instance ADT, but it is anemic: accessConfigs/natIP are still being collapsed into a separate `public_ip` boolean in the service layer, leaving two parallel views of the same upstream data. Recommended changes: align naming and CHANGELOG; specify MANUAL in metadata or drop it; move GKE-detection onto the Instance ADT as `is_gke_managed`; enrich NetworkInterface to subsume the public-IP derivation; document or remove the zero-NIC branch and test it.
